title.narrative: ITP 295 Media Development in a Democratic Framework Georgia
ITP 295 Självreglerande ramverk för demokratisk mediautveckling Georgien

description.narrative:
1) Individuals and organisations participating in the programme benefit from and leverage networks in terms of media regulatory and self-regulatory frameworks. These networks include national contacts in Georgia, collaborations with key actors in Sweden (as an EU Member State) and cooperation with relevant European institutions.
2) Increased knowledge and capacity to initiate and implement structured, long-term transformation work within the participants' respective organizations.
3) That the participants, individually and together as a team, through a collaborative process in which key actors generate and develop ideas and actions adapted to the recommendations put forward by the European Commission on Georgia's candidacy for membership of the European Union.

International Training Programme (ITP): "Self-regulating frameworks for democratic media development". The programme aims at strengthening the capacity of strategically important actors and organisations in Georgia in their work to establish, support and protect self-regulating frameworks for media in support of freedom of speech.

Internationellt kapacitetsutvecklingsprogram (ITP) som syftar till att stärka strategiskt viktiga aktörer och organisationer i Georgien i deras arbete att etablera, stötta och skydda institutioner som ingår i yttrandefrihetens självreglerande ramverk, genom att aktivt tillämpa den teoretiska och praktiska kunskap som erhållits genom programmet. Genomförare är NIRAS Sweden AB, ledningsansvarig part, i konsortium med International Media Support (IMS), Linnéuniversitetet (FOJO: Medieinstitutet) och Global Reporting Sweden AB, som har tilldelats ramavtalet efter upphandling.

sector.narrative: Media and free flow of information

description.narrative:
The results from this ITP programme were affected about the political changes in Georgia during the 12 months period of the programme.
The information below is mainly from the Final report of the programme which includes results from an internal survey done by the programme coordinators.
As a summary, the report states that "However, the extent to which newly acquired knowledge has been used in practice, including the implementation of change initiatives, was significantly affected by the critical political situation caused by the initiation and adoption of the Law on Transparency of Foreign influence in Georgia, as well as the decisive parliamentary elections in October 2024".
"Despite these challenges, the ITP experience is assessed as a valuable and relevant contribution to Georgian media, providing a better understanding of existing best international practices in EU countries. Most respondents believe that the ITP Media met their expectations (to some extent 6 respondents, to a large extent 9 respondents). The programme was positively received for broadening perspectives and facilitating communication and collaboration among participants".
OUTCOME 1 The ITP Media served as a platform for dialogue between home organisations of the participants and other key stakeholders for discussion about media regulation and self-regulation, however the extent varied from a small extent (3 respondents) to medium (6 respondents) and high extent (6 respondents). Through the change initiatives, ITP Media promoted cooperation and team building among different stakeholders.
OUTCOME 2 - Increased knowledge and capacity to initiate and implement structured, long-term transformational work within their respective organisations.
"The knowledge of self-regulation has substantially increased as a result of the ITP Media. Before the ITP Media, only 5 respondents felt they had an understanding to a large extent; this increased to 12 respondents after the programme".
"Due to the participation of highly qualified individuals, some already had a good understanding about media self-regulation before the ITP, however the programme was still considered an added value in terms understanding successful European examples in depth. Accordingly, overall media self-regulation as a method for achieving media freedom has become more preferable among respondents, compared to before ITP. Before the ITP, only 6 participants believed media self-regulation to be highly preferable for media freedom, while afterwards the number increased to 11".
OUTCOME 3 - Participants individually and together as a team, through a multi-stakeholders/ collaborative process, generate and develop ideas, and action points which will align with the recommendations put forth by the European Commission on Georgias EU candidacy.
"The implementation of change initiatives is currently the least visibly changed aspect of the ITP Media. The respondents found it feasible to implement change initiatives to some extent both within their organisations and outside, however the extent of implementation was seriously affected by ongoing political crisis and changed priorities for media organisations".
OUTPUT 1 - Improve the understanding of recent/ proposed legislation in the EU to promote a better implementation in the respective country: AVMSD, Copyright Directive, EMFA, DSA, Political Advertising Regulation, Code of Practice on Disinformation.
"The respondents have considerably increased their knowledge about relevant EU legislation, which was understood as important for both the media environment and their professional growth. Some aspects of EU legislation were explicitly noted several times as especially helpful due to their implications for digital and media sectors, such as the DSA, the DMA, the AVMSD, and EMFA. The respondents also appreciated learning about the rationale behind the legal regulations as well as their practical application by key stakeholders".
OUTPUT 2 - Participants gain an understanding of the intersection between media, freedom of expression, human rights including gender equality, and democracy.
"The ITP has increased respondents understanding about connection between media and freedom of expression, human rights including gender equality and democracy by underlying the importance of allowing diverse and independent voices in the media".
OUTPUT 3 - Participants have access to expanded international and national networks as support for effective work with regulatory and self-regulatory frameworks.
"The respondents have considerably expanded their networks, both nationally and internationally, although the national impact was slightly higher. Networking within the country was perceived as one of the biggest advantages of the programme. A great value was seen in these new connections as a key for effective work on media self-regulation and the majority felt positive about the national network".
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
